newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Sky to buy-out mgt contract from Harrah's.
newsitem.headline: Sky to buy-out mgt contract from Harrah's.

text.p: Sky City Ltd said on Thursday it was to buy out the management contract that Harrah's Entertainment Inc, Memphis, holds for Sky City.
"Sky City will pay a buy-out fee, based on a formula provided in the contract, to Harrah's. The payment is likely to be in the region of NZ$13.5 million after tax," Sky City said in a statement.
Sky City said it currently pays a substantial annual management fee to Harrah's for the operational services provided under the contract.
It said Harrah's would continue to operate the Sky City complex in Auckland for a period of up to 12 months while Sky City completes the legal requirements of obtained the operator's licence.
"The repurchasing of the casino operation by the owners is not uncommon internationally, and the buy-out scenario was anticipated in the original agreement between Sky City and Harrah's," Sky said.

Evan Davies, Managing Director of Sky City said "Our vision for Sky City is to be New Zealand's premier entertainment and leisure facility. The buy-out will bring the business home to Auckland and will create long term shareholder value."
In a separate statement, Brierley Investments Ltd said it had reached agreement with Harrah's to pay NZ$6.75 per share for all of Harrah's shares in Sky City.
The purchase will comprise 12.5 million ordinary shares, or 12.5 percent of the ordinary shares on issue.
Following completion of the deal Brierley will hold 63.1 percent of the ordinary shares in Sky City.
